pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine turning dark port-wine red upon exposure to air and light due to the oxidation of excess porphobilinogen into porphyrins. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic defect caused by a deficiency in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (also known as porphobilinogen deaminase), an enzyme crucial to the heme biosynthetic pathway. When triggered by factors like cytochrome P450-inducing drugs, fasting, or stress, the metabolic pathway becomes overburdened, leading to a toxic accumulation of heme precursors: delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These precursors are neurotoxic, causing autonomic neuropathy (tachycardia, hypertension, abdominal pain), severe peripheral motor neuropathy (ascending weakness), and central nervous system disturbances (psychosis, hyponatremia via SIADH), notably without cutaneous photosensitivity.
